scope: Design only for exact retained direct-RPC fixture workspace. No cleanup executed.
required_preflight: Pin new cleanup manifest to original failed acceptance/manifest/config/source/old binary hashes and the four archived terminal operation request/receipt/log refs, plus exact journal UUID. Verify all four pool device/image/owner identities unchanged.

Require original launcher unit terminal and its worker/runner processes absent; serialize this new action with the fixture control lock. Start only one newly recorded runner using the original byteguard authority/config and same journal, never a worker or new workspace.

Before RPC mutation recheck live journal exactly matches the relevant retained target: sole unreleased lease is that workspace, epoch1/revision1, active_operation empty, all four exact operations terminal with unchanged request/result/receipt, and no prepared/running/unknown operations. Refuse any unexpected workspace/job/journal UUID or unresolved physical state.

This quota fixture has no application PostgreSQL run for its direct-RPC workspace. Do not invent a PG terminal state or fake database-backed cleanup lease. Issue only explicit short-lived operator fixture authority scoped to this tuple and inspect/cancel/snapshot/release; never reuse an expired original grant or add prepare/execute/adopt rights.
stages: Save an exclusive cleanup intent and full pre-observation in a new evidence/logs-01-cleanup directory; preserve logs-01 byte-for-byte, including its failed acceptance.

Call production StopWorkspace at the same epoch and verify the returned same workspace/revision plus NoActiveOperations and the content-addressed stop artifact bytes/pin. No new execution/adoption or epoch increment.

Call production SealSnapshot, read and hash its actual artifact, verify tenant/run/kind/workspace/revision/content and durable journal pin, then archive its bytes and proof before release. Label it a code snapshot. All four log/receipt/disk sidecar evidence must already be preserved and hash checked.

Call production ReleaseWorkspace only after the archived snapshot proof is durable. It removes only identity-checked four terminal containers and the exact workspace storage; require target volume lease released, workspace released, old receipt/request/result rows unchanged and only expected cleanup/pin/stop fields changed. Confirm no active or unknown work.
Stop only the newly launched runner after acknowledged release and retain PID/binary/config/signal identity. Write a separate cleanup result, never replace original failed acceptance.
crash_boundary: Persist and validate each stage. If release outcome is unknown, reobserve the exact UUID/tuple before any next action.

Once workspace released=true or storage removed, do not repeat Stop/Seal (they can be fenced). Require the previously saved verified snapshot proof and retry only the same idempotent ReleaseWorkspace if storage cleanup is incomplete; if proof is missing or identities differ, stop for inspection.
No direct journal edits, Docker force-removal, directory reset, pool rebind, lease refund or reformat.
